# Effect: transient_shaper

Transient shaper: boosts or reduces the attack and sustain separately, regardless of level.

**Where to put it**: Most used on drums: attack_db +4 to +8 makes drums snappier and punchier; sustain_db -6 tightens the tail (removes room sound). Put it before the compressor.

Latest parameters: `muser effects transient_shaper` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attack_db` | 0 | -24 – 24 dB | Attack gain. + punchier, snappier; - softer, more distant |
| `sustain_db` | 0 | -24 – 24 dB | Sustain gain. + more tail and room; - drier and tighter |
| `attack_ms` | 20 | 2 – 200 ms | Length of the attack stage. Drums 5-20 |
| `sustain_ms` | 400 | 60 – 3000 ms | Reaction time of the sustain stage |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "transient_shaper", "attack_db": 6, "sustain_db": -4 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Punchier, crisper drums

  ```json
  {"type": "transient_shaper", "attack_db": 6, "sustain_db": 0}
  ```

- Drier, tighter drums (remove room sound)

  ```json
  {"type": "transient_shaper", "attack_db": 2, "sustain_db": -8}
  ```

- Softer, more distant drums

  ```json
  {"type": "transient_shaper", "attack_db": -6, "sustain_db": 2}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Unlike a compressor, it looks only at the shape of the sound, not the level: a soft hit and a hard hit get the same proportion of processing.
- Put it before the compressor: set the shape first, then control the dynamics.
- It also works on acoustic guitar (plucks become clearer) and bass (attack makes the note onset clearer).
